chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Exchange gifts, you will love one another; exchange gifts, for they remove enmity.'

key_terms.تَحَابُّوا: Love one another / become mutually loving

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and social benefit of exchanging gifts according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith emphasizes the Prophetic tradition of using gift-giving as a practical mechanism to dissolve grudges and cultivate affection, a concept deeply rooted in Shia ethical teachings on social harmony. Scholars note that the repetition of 'tahādaw' (exchange gifts) underscores its importance as a proactive social duty rather than a mere custom, aligning with the Quranic principle of maintaining brotherhood and unity among believers.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, form Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Give gifts, you would find love. Give gifts, you would remove the malice’.
en.sarwar: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ja’far ibn Muhammad from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Kufiy from Al-Husayn ibn Zayd who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘You should exchange gifts of berries; it revives affection and friendship.’”
